title: Add top-k tail-risk canary detector + adaptive quorum rollout guard
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a new Top-K Tail Risk detector that raises canary flags for concentrated latency outliers, plus an adaptive quorum guard to require cross-slice consensus before rollouts proceed.
description:
Context and motivation: We have recurring incidents where small fractions of traffic exhibit severe tail latency (p99.99+) after model or runtime changes. Existing detectors (percentile fusion, temporal cohorts) flag broad regressions but often miss concentrated tail risk that affects a tiny slice yet can cause downstream failures. This PR introduces a Top-K Tail-Risk detector that explicitly measures concentrated extreme latency events across stratified traffic slices and an adaptive quorum rollout guard that requires a configurable fraction of slices to agree on degradation before blocking a rollout.

What this change does: Implements a probabilistic tail-risk scoring algorithm (inspired by EVT-style peak-over-threshold combined with Top-K frequency aggregation) that: 1) computes per-slice extreme-event counts over time windows, 2) normalizes by baseline traffic to surface concentrated bursts, and 3) produces a confidence score and suggested mitigation severity. The adaptive quorum guard consumes these signals and enforces policy rules in the rollout controller: quorum policies are configurable by SLO weight, minimum-slice coverage, and hysteresis cooldown.

Why this approach: Concentrated tail events (e.g., 0.1% of requests with very long latencies) can cascade into queuing amplification and throughput collapse when retries or autoscaling kicks in. By focusing on the Top-K extreme samples and requiring cross-slice consensus, we reduce false positives from noisy single-slice blips while catching real, high-impact regressions earlier.

Compatibility and scope: The detector plugs into the existing perf-canary pipeline (ingest -> slice-aggregator -> detectors -> orchestrator). No changes to runtime inference path are required. Defaults are conservative: detector disabled by default for non-critical deployments and enabled for Dedicated + Private by the rollout config.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector implementation and unit tests (perf-canary/detectors/topk_tail_risk.py + tests)
- [x] Adaptive quorum guard in rollout service (perf-canary/guards/adaptive_quorum_guard.py)
- [x] Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard snippets added (observability/dashboards/topk_tail_risk.json)
- [x] Integration tests for end-to-end signal flow (tests/e2e/test_topk_quorum_flow.py)
- [x] Update docs and config reference (docs/canaries/topk_tail_risk.md)
- [x] Manual smoke in staging with shadow traffic

Summary of commits: 
- feat(detector): add TopK tail-risk detector with threshold scheduling 
- feat(guard): add adaptive quorum guard and policies for rollout controller 
- perf(test): add e2e harness and synthetic traffic generator for tail events 
- docs: add README, dashboard snippets, and configuration examples 

Files changed (high level): 
- perf-canary/detectors/topk_tail_risk.py 
- perf-canary/guards/adaptive_quorum_guard.py 
- perf-canary/scheduler/sampling_scheduler.py (minor change to support burst probes)
- observability/dashboards/topk_tail_risk.json 
- tests/unit/test_topk_tail_risk.py 
- tests/e2e/test_topk_quorum_flow.py 
- docs/canaries/topk_tail_risk.md 
- ci/workflows/canary-e2e.yml (added a staged job)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added and run locally. CI initially failed on an e2e flaky timing assertion (tests/e2e/test_topk_quorum_flow.py) due to environment clock skew in the early build; I adjusted the test to allow timing jitter and re-ran. Final CI: all unit, linters, and e2e gates passed.

Backward compatibility & safety: Feature is gated behind config flags and defaulted off for non-critical namespaces. Guard configuration includes a safe-mode (fail-open) for experimental clusters. No DB migrations.

Follow-ups: 1) Add sampling-weighted baseline update (ENG-3310) 2) Perf-tune probe scheduler for very low-volume slices 3) Add RL-driven quorum tuning experiment in staging.

review_comments: Arjun Rao (reviewer): Nice direction — can you explain how you pick K and the threshold? Concerned about tuning complexity.

Author (Maya): We pick K dynamically as the minimum of fixed-K and top-quantile by traffic (configurable). Thresholds use a rolling peak-over-threshold estimator with a conservative multiplicative band; added comments and examples in docs.
Leah Kim (reviewer): Add more unit tests around low-traffic slices; I saw one flaky e2e run.
